help.Options Menu:
•Preferences:
Opens a window where you can choose the keys used to play, change the sound output volume and select music options (random, selected, none), adjust the overall game speed (choosing the frame rate you wish).

•Use Quickdraw:
Needed to play PacMac if your Mac is equipped with a non-standard video card: it slows down the animation a little.

•Background Tasks:
Allows multitasking during the game. Useful when downloading or compressing files: it may slow down the game, though.

•Use/Remove Musics:
If your Mac is equipped with a 020/030 processor, by default you will have all musics disabled in order to perform smoother animation and better game speed. Anyway, you can activate the musics with this option, so to test your Mac's power in displaying animation, playing sounds and music.
help.Music Menu:
•Musics Background.
To listen to musics while playing, simply put your  MOD, MIDI, MED and/or other format files inside the "Music" folder before launching the game. In order for a music file to be recognized correctly, it has to have the correct "type" ('STrk' for MOD files, 'Midi' for MIDI files and so on). If you open such a file with a specific software such as the holy PlayerPRO by Antoine Rosset, or SoundTrecker or MODPlayer or the like, the file "type" will be automatically assigned.

These are all the available options in the menu:

•Play Next:
Plays the "next" song in the list, or a random one as selected in the Preferences dialog.

•Songs submenu:
To choose which music to play.

•Music On/Off:
Who knows... ;-)

•Cycle:
To choose when to change a music playing.
help.How To Play:
•Really? Never played Pacman(tm)?

OK, after having choosen your preferred music, the way you will play et cetera, you can go on and start PacMac Deluxe.

•The game is just like Pacman(tm), of course.
The purpose is to eat all food (those coloured  dots) in a level, trying not to be catched by the guardians: the ghosts! Obviously, all three kinds of pills are gonna make you invincible for a while: just haunt the ghosts when you swallow a pill, and you'll be able to eat those nasty runners! Keep in mind, though, that a single pill lasts no longer than seven seconds...

The game area is a rectangular grid of 300 cells. Each cell can be empty or not. If a cell is empty or contains a dot or a pill, then the Pac can/must step over it. If a cell contains a wall, regardless of its shape, the Pac can't step over it. This means that sometimes a cell might look free even if it contains a very small brick. Keep your eyes wide open! Examine the map before starting to play and you will have no problems.
help.The Level Editor (continued):
Please remember that if you keep the mouse button down, you'll continue the currently initiated action, e.g. drawing on the grid with the selected piece, or picking up a  piece from the grid or the palette.

•On the right side of the screen there is a set of self-explanatory text buttons.

To erase some pieces from the grid just use the "Select Eraser" option.

Using the Cut and Paste options (from the Edit menu) lets you easily create "sets" of similar levels, by copying and modifying a "basic" level.

•Always test the level you've just created before actually playing it!

The level is completed when all the dots have been actually eaten. If you leave a dot impossible to reach (surrounded by walls in every direction, for example) you won't be able to finish that level. This definitely ain't nice if you're playing your best-record-match!

help.Introduction:
•In the beginning there was the Question.

Is there anyone, in the wonderful world of videogames, who doesn't know of/has never played PacMan(tm), that yellow ball, eating yellow balls, haunted by multicolored ghosts?
For those people (if they really exist) and for those who know it, played it and still want to play it, PacMac Deluxe was born.
OK, another clone, you might think.

•But there's something new.

Wonderful animation, tons of levels, any music modules you wish (three provided), HiRes graphics for 17" and higher monitors and, last but not least, the chance to create your ever-dreamed own levels!
Now, all of this is possible with PacMac Deluxe!
If ya ain't got a Mac (or an Amiga emulating it thru ShapeShifter: yes, Herr Bauer, it works!), then you can't even be reading this nice, little help section.

Before starting to play PacMac Deluxe, please take a look at the menus: they appear or disappear when you toggle the space bar.
help.Standard Menus:
•The Apple menu.

Besides containing your current system items,  it lets you access this help text. 

•The File menu.

It lets you start playing, abort the current game, view the Hall Of Fame and quit PacMac Deluxe.

•The Edit Menu.

It is active only when you are in "Level Editor" mode (available to registered users only).

The usual Cut, Copy, Paste, Clear, Undo functions are relative to the level currently displayed in the editor. You can easily create your basic-standard level, copy it, create new empty levels and then paste it on 'em all,  in order to finish, complete and refine 'em later.
Remember that when you switch to a different level, you lose the contents of the Undo buffer.
help.Options Menu (continued):
•Music in game:
To choose to listen to some musics while playing PacMac.

•Sounds in game:
To hear game sound effects while playing PacMac.

•WakaWaka:
To turn on/off the WakaWaka(tm) tone, the sound you hear when rolling 'round with the Pac.

•Sequential play:
It pops up a window where you can choose the level file and number from which to start playing. Other levels will be explored sequentially, moving automatically from a level file to the next when needed.

•Random play:
It will select the level file and number to be played randomly from ANY level contained in the "Levels" folder and loaded at startup (one file only for unregistered users).
help.LevelEditor Menu:
•Please, read the "Level Editor" section to learn more about the Level Editor.
•This mode is available to registered users only.

•New level file:
Creates a new level file on your disk. This file will contain your new levels (up to 99).

•Edit level file:
Allows to choose the level file to edit. It is not possible to edit default levels (Pac Levels), nor any level file created by a DAPPSofter or an Official Tester.

•Save level file:
Writes the current level file to disk.

•Create level:
Creates a new, empty level at the end of the current level file.

•Next/Previous level:
Goes to next/previous level in file.

•Test current level:
Lets you play the current level, and then return to the Level Editor.
help.The Level Editor:
•Finally, you are now able to draw your own levels to play with.
The tool that DAPPSoft is providing registered users for this purpose is our wonderful Level Editor.

First, you must create a level file (note that you cannot edit the level files you've found in the archive: those are created by our developers and only DAPPSofters or Official Testers can modify them). Each level file can contain up to 99 diferent levels.

On the screen, you'll see a grid made up by 20 x 15 cells representing the game area. Here is where you can put walls, pills to eat ghosts with and coloured dots to eat.

•Anything you need to draw your levels is on the screen.

On the bottom side, there's a palette depicting all the pieces we made to create levels with: walls, dots and pills. All you have to do is to choose the piece you want to use by clicking on it on the palette and start drawing with it on the grid.
You can even "pick up" the pieces directly from the main grid simply by keeping the Option key down when clicking on a piece on the map.
help.Performance:
•By default the game starts with QuickDraw animation.

This is slower than our custom animation code, so if you feel that the game lacks responsiveness, you should definitely try to disable QuickDraw in the Options menu.
Most (but not all) graphic cards work fine with our custom animation code.
Your mileage may vary.

•Playing music is an expensive task.

If your machine cannot play music smoothly, you should play with only sounds on (the default in the Options menu). On some particularly old machines it might even be needed to turn off sounds as well, though this is extremely rare.

Finally, playing at low resolutions like 640x480 might improve things a little.
help.Tips'n'Tricks:
•Remember the door.
You must give the ghosts a door to go in and out of their cage. Look at the levels included in the game and watch the area containing the ghosts in the center of the screen. On the right side, there's a dotted gray line: that's the door, and you MUST put it there in every level you create, or the ghosts (and the eyes when you eat 'em up) will no more be able to enter/exit the cage.

•Do NOT create a "cul de sac" (a tunnel with only one exit/entrance).
It's not fair, and the ghosts might not be able to get out of it!

•Do not create level files with too many levels.
Keeping a maximum of about 20 levels in each file is good advice: this way, you'll enjoy a much nicer "Random" game!

•Eat as many fruits as you can.
Valid not only for PacMac... ;-)

Try to eat all the four ghosts together, without eating a new pill during the effect of the current one: doing that would reset the "progressive points" counter (200 for first ghost and so on), and you'd gain less points for each ghost eaten.
help.Tips'n'Tricks (continued):
The frame rate you choose via the Preferences dialog may go from as low as 25 fps to as high as 100 fps. If you have the dexterity to drive fast, you can play almost always in a "ghosts eaten" situation.

Create a second folder for your levels: this way you can play only the levels contained in the original "Levels" folder (useful if you like the "Random" play mode).

If you're low on memory, try not to use MOD or MIDI files that are very big. Or try to raise the memory partition up to 5Mb (though 3.5Mb or even 3Mb should be enough in most situations).

•Music files are not all the same.
There are dozens of different formats and it is difficult to recognize them all. If the file is damaged or  in a non-standard music format, PacMac Deluxe will simply stay quiet until you choose another valid module. In rare cases, it might hang or quit suddenly.
•So, please, check the modules before putting 'em in the "Music" folder!
Or add them one at a time, to be sure PacMac Deluxe can actually play them without problems.

•Enjoy it!
help.Contest:
•And now for something completely different...

We’re having a little contest here at DAPPSoft.
We’ll publish the best level files created by our customers in a 10-file collection. Anyone can participate in the contest, with the exception of DAPPSoft members and official beta testers.
People whose level files (each containing a minimum of 10 levels and a maximum of 50 levels) are selected will receive FREE registrations for all present and future DAPPSoft games.
The contest ends at midnight Central European Time on July 15, 1999.

•How to submit level files:

Send an email attachment (BinHex only please) to:
•contest@dappsoft.dreamhost.com
Please, send only *small* files, e.g. between 1KB and 4KB. Twentyfive levels are about 2KB compressed, so... be considerate! ;-)
